summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, and gastroparesis was admitted due to hypertensive urgency and altered mental status. He presented with nausea, vomiting, and confusion, with an initial blood pressure of 235/107 mmHg. The elevated blood pressure and volume overload were managed with intravenous nitroglycerin and emergent hemodialysis, which improved his mental status and stabilized his condition. Imaging studies, including head CT and MRI, showed no acute intracranial abnormalities, with findings consistent with chronic changes. His confusion was attributed to metabolic encephalopathy likely exacerbated by hypertension and polypharmacy. Medications were adjusted, including restarting hydralazine, modifying insulin dosing, and changing hiccup management by stopping chlorpromazine and reducing baclofen dose. The patient improved clinically, returned to his baseline mental status, and was discharged home in stable condition with updated medication instructions and follow-up plans.
